newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris to auction off Juppe's former flat.
newsitem.headline: Paris to auction off Juppe's former flat.

text.p: The city-owned Paris flat which brought public opprobium on its tenant, ex-prime minister Alain Juppe, is to be auctioned off, city hall said on Tuesday.
The disclosure two years ago that Juppe was living in the 179 sq metre apartment in a fashionable left-bank district at a knock-down rent tarnished his image.
He was eventually forced to move out to an official residence at his Matignon office to avoid prosecution.

Juppe was paying rent of just over 13,000 francs ($2,280) a month -- about half the market rate -- for the flat which the city hall is offering for auction at a starting price of 5.5 million francs ($970,000).

The disclosures by the satirical weekly le Canard Enchaine that the Gaullist-dominated city hall was letting flats cheaply to political cronies and journalists caused a scandal known as "Chiractown" after President Jacques Chirac, who was mayor for 18 years until May 1995.
Chirac's Gaullists lost control of six of Paris' 20 districts in municipal elections in June 1995 as a result.
